newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bonds rise, German yield gap narrows on CPI.
newsitem.headline: Danish bonds rise, German yield gap narrows on CPI.

text.p: Danish bond prices rose and the 10-year yield differential with Germany narrowed on Wednesday after lower than expected Danish March CPI rises, with dealers predicting further moderate price rises but unsure about the yield gap holding.
Denmark's year-on-year inflation rose 1.7 percent in March compared to analysts' average expectations of 2.1 percent using the Danish national calculation formula.
"The CPI data helped the yield gap narrow, but it is questionable whether this can hold. Prices should nudge up though," one dealer said.

The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was up 0.16 point from the start at 109.58, 0.42 up on Tuesday's close, yielding 6.54 percent in two billion crown turnover, while its June future rose 0.62 point to 109.08 with 55 contracts traded. The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 rose 0.45 point to 87.95.

The crown traded at 3.8099 per mark at 1110 gmt, up from 3.8110 at the opening. The 10-year yield gap with Germany narrowed three basis points to 70. The Central Bank was active on the market selling some 800 million crowns worth of various bonds as part of its routine financing operations.
